rows.description: You feel a hot pang when they laugh with someone else. Wise: name the insecurity behind it and share it as your feeling, not an accusation. Immature: interrogating, demanding passwords or forbidding friends.
They get upset about your friends and you feel watched. Wise: reassure once and hold the line that trust is not shown by surrendering your freedom. Harmful: hiding people to keep the peace.

rows.subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
rows.description: A friend gets the offer or the marks and you feel small while smiling. Wise: admit the envy privately, congratulate honestly, and use it to clarify what you want. Immature: belittling their win.

rows.subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
rows.description: Your success makes a friend distant or sarcastic. Wise: stay warm without hiding your progress, and give them room. Harmful: downplaying yourself to be liked.
My manager backed me when others doubted me and I feel deep gratitude. I honour it with excellence and honesty, and I keep my own judgment; gratitude is not a reason to overlook their mistakes.
A manager gave you a chance when others did not. Feel the gratitude, but also stay honest. Thanks does not mean silence when you see an error; a good manager will value your candid input.

I broke my partner's trust and want the marriage to survive. I accept their anger, answer questions honestly without defensiveness, and let trust return at their pace, not mine; asking to be forgiven quickly repeats the harm.

I discover my partner has been unfaithful and feel shock, nausea, and shaken sense of who I am. It is not my failing. I take time, avoid rash public revenge, lean on trusted people, and decide about the future when calmer.

Thoughts loop on them, you check their profile and mood constantly. Wise: notice it is fantasy feeding on uncertainty, widen your life, talk to a friend. Harmful: tracking their movements or turning up uninvited.
Someone's attention feels intense and unwanted, and you feel uneasy. Wise: say a clear no once, stop replying, keep records, and tell a friend or hostel warden if it continues. It is not your fault.
I cut a corner or hid a decision from my co-founder and now feel uneasy. I come clean early, offer repair, and restore agreements; excuses like it was for the company's good will not rebuild trust.

You realise you wronged your partner and they are hurt. Own it clearly, offer restitution, and accept consequences without demanding forgiveness. Justifying yourself with they did it too keeps the injury alive.
